display_title: A Multimodal artificial intelligence framework for mechanistic discovery and digital twin construction in cardiovascular medicine
summary: This Correspondence discusses a research agenda connecting multimodal biological interpretation with patient-specific simulation in cardiovascular medicine. It sets out design and translation requirements without reporting a newly built, clinically validated digital twin system.
research_question: How can multimodal AI support cardiovascular mechanism research and updateable patient-specific digital models?
author_summary: The Correspondence outlines two linked directions for cardiovascular AI: investigating disease mechanisms and developing patient-specific digital twins. It discusses combining imaging and molecular information to generate network and disease-subtyping hypotheses, then considers updateable physiological models, image-to-mesh workflows and treatment-scenario simulation. Longitudinal data, computational capacity, prospective evaluation, privacy and governance are presented as requirements for translation. This page organizes those narrative arguments for research planning and methodological citation. The cited empirical examples remain evidence from other works; cross-modal integration does not itself establish causation, and simulated treatment scenarios are not observed therapeutic effects in patients.
evidence_page_notice: This evidence page describes a Correspondence. Key Arguments summarize the authors' methodological proposals and narrative discussion, not new experimental findings. Cited studies remain prior evidence; citation-use guidance is this site's interpretation of appropriate scope.
